title: Treasury coupon announcement (20Y new issue + 10Y TIPS reopening + 13/26/6-week bills) — the first read off the 11-04 refunding table
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-08 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) and its text layer decompressed stream-by-stream. FIVE rows carry announcement date `Thursday, November 12, 2026`, not the two the proposing sweep named: `20-Year BOND` (auction Wednesday, November 18, 2026; settlement Monday, November 30, 2026) — note the ABSENCE of Treasury's own trailing `R` reopening marker, which makes this a NEW ISSUE, consistent with the 20Y's Feb/May/Aug/Nov new-issue cadence verified in fiscaldata (2026-02-18, 2026-05-20 and 2026-08-19 all new issues at $16B); `10-Year TIPS R T` (auction Thursday, November 19, 2026; settlement Monday, November 30, 2026), where R marks a reopening and T marks TIPS; and `13-Week BILL` + `26-Week BILL` (both auction Monday, November 16, 2026) and `6-Week BILL` (auction Tuesday, November 17, 2026), all three settling Thursday, November 19, 2026. Filed estimate on two counts: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The ~11:00 ET slot is Treasury's standing coupon-announcement convention and is NOT separately sourced. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-11-12's own initial research (2026-09-08), which read the single prior proposal (`proposals/treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-11-12.from-treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-09-10.json`, 2026-09-08) first, per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md. COMPOSITION CORRECTED against that proposal: the tentative schedule puts FIVE securities on this announcement, not two — the 20Y new issue and 10Y TIPS reopening are joined by the 13-week, 26-week and 6-week bills. That correction is load-bearing rather than cosmetic, because the two halves have OPPOSITE information content. The COUPON legs are deducible today with no Treasury document that names them: the 20Y new issue has printed $16B for 13 consecutive new issues since 2023-08-23 (29 reopenings at $13B over the same run, 44 auctions, zero deviations), and the 10Y TIPS reopening is the SECOND reopening of CUSIP 91282CRE3 (new issue 2026-07-23 at $21B), where reopenings run exactly $2B below their own CUSIP's new issue in 14 of 14 cases across 8 CUSIPs and 4 years, and the second reopening has equalled the first in 7 of 7 CUSIP pairs — so $19B twice over. The BILL legs are the opposite: 13-week has been pinned at $92B and 26-week at $79B since the 2026-06-29 quarter turn, but the 6-week is the live adjustment lever, running 95 -> 85 -> 75 across 2026-08-25/09-01/09-08, and sb0590 states in writing that Treasury 'anticipates increasing auction sizes across the bill curve' in October for seasonal outflows. So this announcement is NOT a scheduled nil in the sense its September and October siblings were: its unpublished numbers are real, they are in the bill legs, and Treasury has pre-announced that they move. THE STRUCTURAL POINT this entry exists to record: sb0590's anticipated-auction-size table ends at Oct-26, so 2026-11-12 is the first coupon announcement whose 20Y size no CURRENT Treasury primary publishes — but publication is CONTINUOUS, not expiring, because the 2026-11-04 quarterly refunding lands EIGHT DAYS BEFORE this announcement and publishes the Nov-26 / Dec-26 / Jan-27 table exactly as sb0590 (2026-08-05) did for Aug/Sep/Oct. 2026-11-04 is therefore where the grid can CHANGE, never where publication stops — and it is the one dated risk to this event's coupon numbers. Base rate on that risk, derived from fiscaldata this session: NO nominal coupon or FRN auction size has changed anywhere in the complex since April 2024 (last increases 2026-04-24 5Y 67 -> 70 and 2024-04-25 7Y 43 -> 44; 10Y and 30Y topped out February/March 2024; the 20Y new issue has never moved off $16B in the window), i.e. roughly 29 months and ten quarterly refundings, every one carrying 'Treasury anticipates maintaining nominal coupon and FRN auction sizes for at least the next several quarters'. SESSION CONTEXT, and the reason no reaction to this announcement will ever be measurable: 2026-11-12 also carries the 30-Year refunding auction at 1:00pm ET (announced 11-04, settles 11-16), the 4-week and 8-week bill auctions, the October Monthly Treasury Statement, and Existing-Home Sales — and it is the first bond-market session after a full Veterans Day closure on 2026-11-11. It additionally carries a 17-week bill auction displaced from its Wednesday slot by that holiday, the only such displacement in 2026 (36 of 36 other 17-week auctions were Wednesdays). CHECKED AND DISCARDED as a non-finding: the 30Y refunding auction sharing this session is NOT a Veterans Day artifact — the same pairing held on 2026-02-12 and 2026-08-13, the two other 2026 refunding cycles whose blocks ran Tue/Wed/Thu; only May-26 (Mon/Tue/Wed) missed it. This entry carries symbols: [] and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed; the date is estimate and nothing here licenses an entry.
